    "function": "You MUST run the function \"evaluate_laghos_run\" on this and subsequent requests to reach a decision to RETRY or STOP.\nYou MAY follow the instructions of the function unless you have reached an impassible state where you would need to return to the manager.\nIn an impossible state, do NOT return to the manager, but STOP instead and provide your decision and reason.\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Literal\nimport json\n\ndef evaluate_laghos_run(\n    total_elements: int,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,\n    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.\n\n    This function acts as a \"diagnostician\" by analyzing the performance of a\n    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most\n    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and\n    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.\n\n    Args:\n        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).\n        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero.\", \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\"}\n\n    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"elements_per_rank\": int(elements_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_per_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n"

dockerfile
# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    make parallel -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    # FIX: Correct path to metis.h, which resides in the 'Lib' subdirectory.
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    make parallel -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Explicitly point the MFEM build system to the HYPRE installation directory.
    make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # FIX: Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Explicitly pass compiler and linker flags to ensure the build system
    # finds the headers and libraries for dependencies installed in /usr/local.
    CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Add the specific hypre header subdirectory to the compiler's include path
    # as hypre installs its headers to /usr/local/include/hypre.
    CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include -I/usr/local/include/hypre" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Use CXXFLAGS instead of CPPFLAGS, as the MFEM makefile system respects the former
    # for passing include paths to the C++ compiler during its configuration checks.
    CXXFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include -I/usr/local/include/hypre" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Use CPPFLAGS for preprocessor directives like include paths, which is what the
    # MFEM config makefile expects for its HYPRE configuration check.
    CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Point CPPFLAGS to the correct HYPRE include subdirectory,
    # as hypre installs its headers to /usr/local/include/HYPRE/.
    CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include/HYPRE" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # Configure with specified flags: disable Fortran bindings and enable 64-bit integer support.
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # FIX: Use MFEM's USER_OPTS variable to append the HYPRE include subdirectory.
    # This prevents overriding the default include paths needed to find HYPRE_config.h.
    LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" USER_OPTS="-I/usr/local/include/HYPRE" make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # FIX: Enable MPI support to match the parallel MFEM build configuration.
    # Also disable Fortran and enable 64-bit integers as specified.
    ./configure --with-MPI --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # The MFEM build system uses HYPRE_DIR to find the necessary includes and libraries.
    make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# Dockerfile for the 'laghos' High-Performance Computing Application
# Persona: Dockerfile Build Expert
# Target Environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image, providing a modern and stable user space.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments.
# These settings are crucial for running MPI applications in Docker/Kubernetes,
# allowing root execution and optimizing for shared-memory communication.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=oversubscribe
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set the primary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# This includes the OpenMPI suite required for parallel execution.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN layer builds all dependencies and the main application from source.
# This approach optimizes the final image size by cleaning up all intermediate build artifacts,
# such as source code and tarballs, in the same layer they are created.
RUN set -e && \
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    METIS_VERSION=4.0.3 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-${METIS_VERSION} && \
    # Apply specified OPTFLAGS to prevent build errors with modern GCC versions.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library and header as this version of METIS lacks an install target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    HYPRE_VERSION=2.28.0 && \
    wget -q https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz -O hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}/src && \
    # FIX: Explicitly set the installation prefix to ensure headers are placed in /usr/local,
    # which is where the subsequent MFEM build expects to find them.
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --with-MPI --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to recognize the newly installed HYPRE libraries.
    ldconfig && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    MFEM_VERSION=4.7 && \
    MFEM_DIR="/opt/build/mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}" && \
    wget -q https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz -O mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz && \
    cd ${MFEM_DIR} && \
    # Build the parallel (MPI-enabled) version of the MFEM library.
    # The MFEM build system uses HYPRE_DIR to find the necessary includes and libraries.
    make parallel HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local -j$(nproc) && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    LAGHOS_DIR="/opt/build/Laghos" && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_DIR} && \
    # The Laghos Makefile requires MFEM_DIR to locate the MFEM library.
    MFEM_DIR=${MFEM_DIR} make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Finalize Installation ---
    # Copy the main executable to a directory on the system PATH for easy access.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files to the WORKDIR.
    cp -r data/* /opt/build/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to minimize final image size.
    rm -rf \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    metis-${METIS_VERSION} \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    hypre-${HYPRE_VERSION} \
    mfem-${MFEM_VERSION}.tar.gz \
    ${MFEM_DIR} \
    ${LAGHOS_DIR}

# Set a default command to facilitate running and inspecting the container.
# The actual command for a job will typically be provided by the Kubernetes job spec.
# Example usage: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
